clue.text: Workforce constructing numerous arches

indicators.note: constructing means building something new out of these two words' letters

explanation.surface: A building crew is busy putting up a whole row of arches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructing' is the anagram signal: the fourteen letters of NUMEROUS and ARCHES are rebuilt into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's staff, and the department that manages them, go by this name; both are its workforce.

clue.text: Kinky items are more erotic

indicators.note: kinky means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the next two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Saucy objects are said to be the raunchier kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' is the anagram signal, and its saucy sense matches the definition so well that it hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy is slang for sexy or passionate, so the comparative means more erotic.

clue.text: Measure boundary

explanation.surface: A short instruction to measure out a boundary line.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete is to measure or deal out, and an old noun mete means a limit or boundary stone, as in metes and bounds.

clue.text: Rubbish youngster picked up, given order

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the word for a child reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a kid is a youngster
tat is cheap rubbish or junk

explanation.surface: A child collects some litter after being told to.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'picked up' means read upwards, so the child word turns to DIK; 'given' only links. A diktat is a German loanword.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree imposed without consent, an authoritarian command.

clue.text: A space like this will accommodate a new plant

indicators.note: will accommodate means the first group of pieces makes room for a pair of letters inside it

parts.note: a gap is a space
thus means like this, in this way

explanation.surface: A gardener says a gap of this size will fit a newly bought plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a gardener's remark; 'will accommodate' slips AN into the outer string, between its second and third pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The agapanthus, or African lily, is a garden plant with blue flower heads.

clue.text: Vocal style used by Lothario sometimes

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A seducer occasionally adopts a particular manner of singing to woo.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lothario is a womaniser; the answer runs across 'LothARIO SOmetimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arioso is an operatic singing manner between recitative and aria, a melodious style of vocal delivery.

clue.text: How to identify criminal, using digital process?

definitions.text: How to identify criminal, using digital process?

parts.words: How to identify criminal, using digital process?
parts.note: the phrase means to inform on or identify a wrongdoer, while 'digital' points at a literal finger, and at fingerprinting

explanation.surface: A question about how police pin down an offender, perhaps by fingerprints.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify someone to the police is idiomatically to point a digit at them, a slang phrase for informing.

clue.text: Clutching book, saunter casually in protected areas of land

indicators.note: clutching means holding on to something, so the rearranged walk letters wrap round the synonym for book
casually means in a loose, unplanned way, so the letters of saunter are rearranged

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Someone strolls through a park carrying a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' makes NATURES from the stroll word; 'Clutching' wraps it round the booking word just before its final S. 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservation sites set aside for wildlife are protected tracts of countryside.

clue.text: Scottish solicitor left worker to collect money

indicators.note: to collect means the insect's letters gather the pay synonym inside them

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
a wage is money paid for work

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer leaves an employee to go and pick up some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' sets the pay word inside the insect; a law agent is a term used only in Scots law.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a solicitor or legal practitioner was formerly called by this title.

clue.text: Expert not put out quickly

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or knocked out of place, so the word not is rearranged

explanation.surface: A professional who refuses to be flustered works fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for at once, with speed, borrowed from Spanish.

clue.text: Being in charge of court case is difficult

definitions.text: Being in charge of court case

explanation.surface: Presiding over a lawsuit is hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hearing a case is said to be trying it, and a trying day is a hard or exasperating one.

clue.text: Take great risk? Attack financial adviser, if running short

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them

indicators.note: running short means the word comes up one letter short at its end

parts.note: a stockbroker advises on and handles investments

explanation.surface: Someone advised to stake everything is tempted to assault the adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if running short' cuts the last letter from BROKER (financial adviser), leaving the word for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk everything on one venture is an idiom for an all-out gamble.

clue.text: Second of items on radio broadcast concerning Indian cooking

indicators.note: second of means take the second letter of the word that follows
this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Something on a radio programme about Indian cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second of' takes T from 'items'; 'broadcast' scatters ON and RADIO to give ANDOORI.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of Indian cuisine cooked in a clay oven, as in the chicken dish.

clue.text: On street there's widespread trouble

parts.note: rife means common or widespread

explanation.surface: Unrest is breaking out all along a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or discord, a state of trouble between people.

clue.text: Youngster — son to hold, right?

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to have is to hold or possess

explanation.surface: A parent is asked whether their son is to be held.
explanation.walkthrough: A young shaver is an old-fashioned word for a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaver is a dated informal word for a boy or young lad.

clue.text: Very bad times for small communities

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects
ages are long eras or times

explanation.surface: Life in small settlements is said to have been grim for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Villages are rural settlements, smaller than towns.

clue.text: One mutters about double quantity of alcohol being passed round

indicators.note: passed round suggests turning, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a double quantity means the drink is taken twice

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A drinker grumbles about a double measure being handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double quantity of' gives RUMRUM; 'being passed round' turns RE + RUMRUM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks in a low indistinct voice is a mumbler, which is one who mutters.

clue.text: Bird suffering pain when wings are cut off

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges of the word, so its first and last letters go

parts.note: smarting means stinging or suffering pain

explanation.surface: A bird is hurting after having its wings clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first and last letters from SMARTING (suffering pain) leaves the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The martin is a small swallow-like bird, such as the house martin.

clue.text: Snub expert in religious studies?

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject in Britain
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: A question about a specialist in theology.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the British school subject covering religious studies; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a curt rejection, the same as a snub.

clue.text: News story creating sensation? Just a little

explanation.surface: A reporter's scoop makes waves, if only a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a front-page story given big treatment, and a splash of milk is a small amount.

clue.text: Musician who achieves his goal?

parts.note: a composer writes music for films, while a striker in football puts the ball in the net

explanation.surface: A composer who succeeds at what they set out to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes or arranges music shares a title with the player who gets a goal.

clue.text: Dance to a dull collection of melodies

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
dry means dull or boring

explanation.surface: Going to a dance only to find it tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Balladry is ballads as a body of songs, a gathering of simple tunes.

clue.text: Wild animal spotted in golf course, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A wildcat is seen roaming a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted in' links; a links is a seaside golf course, especially in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears.

clue.text: Inclined to steal, like a child who eats sweets?

definitions.text: like a child who eats sweets?

explanation.surface: A thieving child who also loves candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is said to have light or tacky fingers, and a child eating candy literally has gluey hands.
